diffs.diff: temperature_C: datasheet reading gives -91.743 per count, the part's model has 1
diffs.evidence: Same transfer function, different units/representation. The second reading's T = -91.743 x V(volts) + 192.94 is just the inverse of the datasheet's linear approximation, Equation 6: 'V = (-10.9 mV/C) x T + 2103 mV' (two-point line over 20-50 C; 1/0.0109 = 91.743, 2103/10.9 = 192.94). The datasheet calls this 'an even less accurate linear approximation' and says the response 'does have a slight umbrella parabolic shape. This shape is very accurately reflected in Table 7-1.' The model's analog-sensor slider is the OUT voltage itself (scale 1 V/V, 0.42-2.616 V, matching Table 7-1's 420 mV at 150 C and 2616 mV at -50 C), and the driver converts the voltage to C by interpolating Table 7-1. Both agree: for example, 1.668 V gives 40 C in Table 7-1 and -91.743 x 1.668 + 192.94 = 39.9 C. No change needed.
